title: Early spring dates gave no clear link to missing autumn colour records in four Swiss beech samples, 1961-2020
abstract: We tested whether earlier recorded beech leaf unfolding predicted a missing autumn colour record at the same station. We used 5,379 spring station-years in western and eastern Switzerland in 1961-1990 and 1991-2020. There were 461 missing autumn records. Four linear probability models controlled station and year effects. Estimates ranged from -0.49 to +2.62 percentage points per ten days earlier spring. All four 98.75 percent cluster intervals included zero. Checks that added other autumn reporting, restricted records to active autumn years, changed time controls or required more complete series also gave intervals that included zero. This audit does not establish that selection bias is small. It tests recorded timing, not temperature, and excludes years with no spring record. Unknown visits, tree changes and one shared network limit inference. Source data overlap prior campaign studies. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate results and a figure permit reproduction.

display.caption: Missing autumn colour slope per ten days earlier recorded spring. Each line is a 98.75 percent cluster interval. Other autumn reporting checks do not establish a clear common link. Source: MeteoSwiss.
